messages:
beth: ACME POC update — customer swapped in a new API key and now getting 401s on every call. They hit us in the test environment around 15:21 UTC. Can we triage?

sam: thanks. do we have the raw curl they used and the response body? usually this is either a key bound to the wrong org/project or a scope mismatch.

beth: customer pasted this: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -H \"Authorization: Bearer ak_live_XXXX\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'` — response is `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid credentials"}`. no extra headers.

jamal: quick check from infra logs: found matching request_id 0a7f3c. auth service logged: `warn auth: failed binding tenant=acme-corp token=ak_live_XXXX err=invalid_org_binding`

sam: ah — token seems to be bound to org `acme` (short name) while customer is sending org context implicitly by project header defaulting to `acme-corp`. if no explicit `x-rw-org` they might be relying on account-level metadata which changed when they rotated key.

tyler: short-term workaround: ask them to set the header `x-rw-org: acme` (or use the token that is bound to `acme-corp`). example curl to test: 
```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer ak_live_XXXX\" \\n  -H \"x-rw-org: acme\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}'
```

mira: customer also asked about pricing if they need Dedicated for consistent throughput during the POC. I told them ballpark: dedicated starts at $Xk/month and includes reserved capacity + SLA; we should confirm exact tier + any overage terms before quoting.

beth: noted — i'll loop in AE for pricing. for now need the auth fix so they can run canaries.

jamal: dug deeper — token metadata shows this key was issued with `allowed_orgs: [\"acme\"]` and `scopes: [\"generate:basic\"]`. two failure modes here: 1) customer is calling with a project whose canonical org is `acme-corp` (mismatch), or 2) the call needs `generate:chat` scope if they use streaming chat endpoints. logs show invalid_org_binding not invalid_scope though.

auth-bot: automated: token-rotation detected for key_id=ak_live_XXXX at 2026-03-20T15:19:58Z. rotation origin=console (user=beth@redwood).

sam: can you ask them to run the curl with the `x-rw-org` header first and paste the full response + request-id? that'll tell us whether it's binding mismatch. also confirm if they use any proxy that might strip headers.

beth: sent this to customer, they replied that they're using a short-lived proxy and will try. also they asked whether creating a second key scoped to both `acme` and `acme-corp` is a valid quick fix.

jamal: yes that's valid — create a service key and add both allowed_orgs entries, or update the project's canonical org alias to include the token's org. long-term we should suggest binding by project id instead of readable org slug.

tyler: ops note — if we enable an alias, ensure we add an audit entry and TTL. i can push a quick alias change for the POC after confirmation from security.

mira: security questionnaire item: customer asks if keys can be restricted by scope and org — answer: yes, keys support per-scope and per-org restrictions; include snippet for the questionnaire?

sam: paste this into questionnaire: `keys support allowed_orgs + allowed_projects + scopes; rotating keys is recommended; RBAC via workspace admin.`

beth: customer ran the curl with `x-rw-org: acme` and it succeeded — they posted request_id=0a7f3c and got 200. they thanked us and asked about the safe cleanup of the original key.

jamal: recommend rotate and revoke the old key after the new key is validated. set TTL on the temporary key to 48h. i'll create the short-lived alias change ticket and tag it `poc-acme` so it's easy to revert.

beth: perfect. AE here for pricing: @mira please confirm dedicated quote and I'll share next steps.

mira: will confirm quote by EOD. happy path restored. :thumbsup:
